rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act - Notice Requirements
rules.requirement: Landlords must provide tenants with a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources when starting the eviction process or deciding not to offer a lease renewal. The notice must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to Quit. Landlords and foreclosing owners must also send a copy of the Notice to Quit or Notice of Non-renewal of Lease, together with a Certificate of Compliance/Service, to the City of Boston's Office of Housing Stability.
rules.citation: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act (HSNA), Ordinance passed October 2020, effective November 6, 2020; Sec. 10-11.7
rules.quoted_span:
The HSNA requires that landlords give this Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources
to tenants when the landlord starts the eviction process, or when the landlord
decides to not offer the tenant a renewal of their lease agreement. The Notice of
Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to
Quit.
rules.key_value: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources must accompany Notice to Quit or Notice of Non-renewal
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to all landlords/foreclosing owners in City of Boston intending to end a tenancy or post-foreclosure occupancy of a residential unit. Does not apply to properties in hospitals, skilled nursing facilities, health facilities, or non-profit substance abuse treatment facilities.
rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; residences in non-profit facility whose primary purpose is providing short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug, or other substance abuse. Requirements may not be waived by lease, contract, or other agreement.
rules.sanctions: First offense: Warning. Second and subsequent offenses: $300 per day. Enforced by Inspectional Services Department. Violation does not halt eviction process.
